output: I recommend we replace NoteBase with Quill: its search is markedly faster, it supports markdown export (solving our current “no export” issue), and at £6/user/month for our 12-person team (£72/month total) it remains cost-effective. We’ll need to confirm its hosting meets our UK-region data residency requirement, but overall Quill offers the performance and functionality improvements we need.
Search in Release 4.2 is now twice as fast on large libraries, and you can export your data to CSV. We’ve also fixed a rare startup crash to make the app more reliable.
The regional figures sum to 120 + 95 + 60 + 55 = 330 (GBP 000s), not 350. The reported total is therefore incorrect (off by 20 GBP 000s).

1. Supplier: deliver the audited accounts – within 30 days of the period end  
2. Client: pay undisputed invoices – within 14 days of receipt

Supported by the sources  
• In the 2019 company trial (Source A), staff self-reported feeling more productive under a four-day week.  
• In the 2022 pilot of 20 people with no control group (Source B), measured output per week remained roughly unchanged.  

Not established by the sources  
• That a four-day week objectively raises overall output.  
• That self-reported productivity gains translate into higher measurable output.  
• Any causal link between the four-day week and increased output (no control group or robust design).  
• Generalizability beyond the single company trial and the small, uncontrolled 20-person pilot.

I recommend adopting Quill for our documentation needs: its significantly faster search and built-in Markdown export address NoteBase’s shortcomings, it meets our UK-only data residency requirement, and at GBP 6 per user per month for our 12-member team, it delivers clear ROI with manageable costs while streamlining operations.
